These engagements provide participants with practical insights into public administration and evidencebased policymaking.

3.1.8 Tamil Nadu Policy and Governance Experiential Centre (TNPAGE)

Tamil Nadu Policy and Governance Experiential Centre (TNPAGE) was established at a cost of Rs.12.65 crore (Rs.10.00 crore under TANII fund and remaining Rs.2.65 crore from Service/Commitment Charges). The Tamil Nadu Policy and Governance Experiential Centre (TNPAGE) was inaugurated on 28.02.2026.

TNPAGE aims to transform governance into an interactive and dynamic process, enabling Government departments to test interventions, explore scenario-based policy modelling and drive

81

data-driven decision-making with unprecedented precision.

TNPAGE is first of its kind Governance Knowledge and Experiential Centre, designed as a public knowledge space that presents Government policies, development indicators and governance outcomes in an immersive and accessible format.

The Centre also includes the Tamil Nadu Policy Portal - the Strategy Room at TNPAGE will serve as a dedicated space for policy discussions, planning and collaborative decision making, supported by advanced data visualisations and analytical tools. Through interactive dashboards, maps and thematic visualisations, it enables policymakers and researchers to explore key socio-economic indicators, track development trends and gain insights that support informed and evidence-based policy formulation for Tamil Nadu.

3.1.9 Transformation of Aspirational Districts Programme

Transformation of Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP) was launched by NITI Aayog in

82

January 2018. The objectives of Aspirational Districts Programme are:

(i) To improve the socio-economic status of 112 identified backward districts,

(ii) To focus on the strengths of each district, and

(iii) To prioritize the attainable outcomes for immediate improvement.

The Districts of Virudhunagar and Ramanathapuram from Tamil Nadu have been selected for implementation of the programme.

3.1.9.1 Focus Areas

The Core focus areas of the Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP) are Health & Nutrition, Education, Agriculture & Water Resources, Financial Inclusion & Skill Development and Basic Infrastructure. Districts are encouraged to become one of the best in the country by competing with and learning from others in the spirit of Competitive Federalism.

83

3.1.9.2 Real time Monitoring and Ranking

The programme is being monitored through the 49 Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) on a monthly basis by NITI Aayog. Based on the performance, the Districts are being ranked on overall and sectoral performance.

is therefore not merely a welfare benefit but

a social enabler and an economic asset — it

The Whole-of-Government approach is further reflected in inter-departmental convergence initiatives, such as integrated responses to skill development, youth employment, gender equity, climate resilience and urban governance. Programmes like Thiranagam demonstrate how multiple departments, institutions, and delivery mechanisms work together within a unified governance framework to address complex, cross-cutting challenges. The use of shared digital

27

platforms, harmonised data systems and regular high-level reviews, reinforce accountability and collective ownership of SDG outcomes. To this end, the departments are evaluated based on measurable service delivery outcomes and citizen experience indicators.

From an SDG lens, Tamil Nadu’s Whole-of- Government (WoG) approach transforms the Goals into a governance framework embedded within the State’s planning and implementation machinery, ensuring policy coherence, efficient use of public resources and consistency across departments.

By institutionalising coordination, strengthening monitoring systems and aligning sectoral actions with long-term development priorities, the State reinforces its commitment to inclusive growth, social justice and the principle of “Leave No One Behind,” positioning the SDGs as a core driver of public policy rather than a parallel agenda.

2.1.7 Whole of Society Approach

The Government of Tamil Nadu has adopted a Whole-of-Society (WoS) approach as a central

28

strategy for advancing the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), recognising that achieving the 2030 Agenda requires collective action beyond Government alone. Anchored in the principle that development outcomes are strongest when State institutions, local Governments, the private sector, civil society, academia, communities and citizens act in convergence, Tamil Nadu’s SDG strategy emphasises collaboration, co-creation, and shared responsibility.

At the institutional level, mechanisms such as SDGCC and the State Planning Commission enable horizontal and vertical coordination across departments while engaging with NGOs. Platforms like Mission Inaippagam, the State’s CSR matchmaking portal, operationalise this approach by aligning private sector CSR investments with State SDG priorities, thereby mobilising corporate resources for public good. Similarly, partnerships with UN agencies, academic institutions, industry bodies and civil society organisations, support knowledge exchange, innovation and implementation capacity.

29

At the local and community level, initiatives such as Urban Social Innovation Platforms, participatory planning processes and people-centric policy designs ensure that citizens are active stakeholders in development rather than passive beneficiaries. Flagship programmes such as Thiranagam demonstrate how inter-departmental coordination, digital systems and partnerships with skilling institutions and industry can coalesce to address youth employability and livelihoods. The State’s emphasis on gender equity, inclusion and social justice further reinforces the WoS approach by prioritising women’s participation, community care systems and safe public spaces as enablers of sustainable growth.

4.4.13 Rainwater Harvesting and Groundwater Recharge

Rainwater harvesting is an essential

component of sustainable urban water

management and has been made mandatory for

buildings through the relevant provisions of the

Tamil Nadu Urban Local Bodies Act, 1998 and the

applicable Building Rules. Its widespread adoption

has contributed significantly to groundwater

159

recharge, improved water availability and greater

resilience against seasonal water scarcity.

Town Panchayats are taking sustained

measures to ensure the effective functioning of

rainwater harvesting systems in residential,

commercial, institutional and Government

buildings. Existing structures are being inspected,

restored and maintained, while the installation of

new systems is facilitated in buildings where

adequate arrangements are not available.

Particular emphasis is placed on rooftop rainwater

collection, recharge pits, percolation wells and

other locally appropriate recharge structures.

Rainwater harvesting is also being

integrated with the restoration of ponds, lakes,

wells, feeder channels and other traditional water

systems to enhance groundwater replenishment

and reduce surface runoff. Town Panchayats

continue to undertake awareness campaigns,

community outreach and capacity-building

160

programs to encourage citizens, institutions and

commercial establishments to conserve rainwater

and maintain harvesting structures effectively.
